changelog: v35 alerting bug-fix release (v36). Three defects in v35's SD-card alerting, all found before this release reached more than one device (cytechoffice-1): (1) packages/cytech.yaml referenced the SMTP credentials as !secret cytech_smtp_* directly, so on ANY device without those keys in secrets.yaml the config failed to parse and the device went to recovery mode -- and because a parseable config is what the maintenance pass that writes the secrets needs to run, it could never recover on its own: a deadlock, hit on cytechoffice-1. Fixed: the two smtp notify platforms moved OUT of cytech.yaml into a device-local packages/cytech_email.yaml that ensure_email_secrets() generates with literal values from the device's /config/.cytech_secrets (chmod 600, byte-compared, only rewritten on change). No credentials file -> no generated file -> nothing references a missing secret -> the config always parses. Fix for devices already deadlocked: the next update pull applies v36; cytech.yaml then parses without recovery mode on the following core start. (2) The smtp notify configs used "encryption: ssl" -- invalid in HA 2026 (must be tls), so the notify services were dropped even with credentials present; the generated package uses tls. (3) The three alert automations and the System Health dashboard cards referenced entity ids that never exist (sensor.cytech_sdcard_result / cytech_canary_result / cytech_boot_result -- HA slugs the sensors' name: fields to sensor.cytech_sd_card_status / cytech_sd_canary / cytech_boot_status), so card rows showed "entity not found" and the alert automations could never trigger; v36 corrects every reference to the live ids. No owner action needed: v35 owners who already have CY_SMTP_* keys in /config/.cytech_secrets get the email package generated on the next pass. Owners who want email alerts for the first time: put CY_SMTP_USER / CY_SMTP_PASS / CY_SMTP_RECIPIENT (KEY=VALUE lines) into /config/.cytech_secrets on the device; ensure_email_secrets() picks them up on its next run. Otherwise v36 continues to add only the SD-card trouble detection from v35 (boot-event recording + restart-storm flag, kernel-journal SD error scan, 8 MB write/read canary, the three status sensors, an alert automation + in-app notification on failure -- the alert simply has no email destination until credentials are set up).
